content:
Given the information that I am going to share:
 1) the full text of the publication that you have to extract grant and funding information from.

Please return a JSON object with a "grants" key containing an array of objects where each object has the following structure:
- `funder_name`: The name of the ONE funding organization or agency. If not found, set it to "n/a".
- `grant_numbers`: An array of grant/award/contract numbers from this SAME funder, to this same recipient. Each grant number is its own array element -- never join several numbers into one comma/semicolon-separated string. If none found, set it to ["n/a"].
- `funding_context_from_paper`: The relevant text passage that mentions this funder and/or grant. If not found, set it to "n/a".
- `recipient`: The author or institution that received the grant. If not found, set it to "n/a".

Please follow these strict instructions:
- The output must be a valid JSON object with a "grants" key.
- The "grants" value must be an array of objects.
- Each object must contain the keys `funder_name`, `grant_numbers`, `funding_context_from_paper`, and `recipient`.
- Every object must represent exactly ONE funder and ONE recipient. If a passage names multiple different funders (even for the same recipient), create a separate object per funder.
- If one funder gave several grant numbers to the same recipient, list them all inside the single `grant_numbers` array of one object -- do not create duplicate objects and do not concatenate the numbers into one string.
- An institution/site name that is merely administering or hosting a grant (e.g. a university running an NIH-funded center) is the `recipient`, not the `funder_name` -- do not set funder_name to that institution's own name.
- Any other output format will be considered invalid.

Below is the input data that you will use to generate the output:
1) content => {content}.
